title: Sucralose Promotes Benzo(a)Pyrene-Induced Renal Toxicity in Mice by Regulating P-glycoprotein.
authors: Hu, Jun; Feng, Ji; Bai, Yan; Yao, Zhi-Sheng; Wu, Xiao-Yu; Hong, Xin-Yu; Lu, Guo-Dong; Xue, Kun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究三氯蔗糖与苯并芘共暴露通过P-糖蛋白调控加重肾毒性，虽涉及分子对接和转录因子表达，但核心是毒理学表型，非蛋白质-DNA互作建模或TF-DNA结合机制研究。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sucralose and benzo(a)pyrene (B[a]P) are widespread foodborne substances known to harm human health. However, the effects of their combined exposure on kidney function remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the mechanisms by which sucralose and B[a]P induce kidney injury through P-glycoprotein (PGP/ABCB1), a crucial protein involved in cellular detoxification. METHODS: C57BL/6N mice were co-treated with sucralose and B[a]P for 90 days to evaluate their impact on kidney histopathology and function. In vitro experiments assessed cell viability, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and B[a]P accumulation by flow cytometry. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) were used to determine the binding affinity of sucralose to PGP. Furthermore, PCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry were performed to analyze the expression of PGP and its upstream transcription factors. RESULTS: Ninety days of co-exposure to sucralose and B[a]P significantly exacerbated renal dysfunction in mice, as evidenced by the elevated level of serum creatinine and urea nitrogen, which could be reverted by ROS scavenger N-acetyl cysteine (NAC). In vitro, sucralose promoted cellular accumulation of B[a]P, consequently enhancing B[a]P-induced cell growth inhibition and ROS production. Consistently, B[a]P accumulation was enhanced by PGP knockdown in both HK2 and HEK-293 cells. Mechanistically, sucralose can directly bind to PGP, competitively inhibiting its efflux capacity and increasing intracellular B[a]P retention. Prolonged co-exposure further downregulated PGP expression, possibly through the reductions of its transcriptional regulators (PXR, NRF2, and NF-kappaB). CONCLUSIONS: Co-exposure to sucralose and B[a]P exacerbates renal injury by impairing PGP function. Mechanistically, sucralose inhibits PGP activity, resulting in the accumulation of B[a]P within renal cells. This accumulation triggers oxidative stress and inhibits cell growth, which demonstrates that sucralose potentiates B[a]P-induced nephrotoxicity by directly inhibiting PGP-mediated detoxification pathways, thus underscoring the critical need to evaluate toxicity risks associated with combined exposure to these compounds.
abstract_zh: 背景：三氯蔗糖和苯并(a)芘（B[a]P）是广泛存在的食源性物质，已知对人体健康有害。然而，它们联合暴露对肾功能的影响仍不清楚。本研究旨在探讨三氯蔗糖和B[a]P通过P-糖蛋白（PGP/ABCB1）——一种参与细胞解毒的关键蛋白——诱导肾损伤的机制。方法：C57BL/6N小鼠经三氯蔗糖和B[a]P联合处理90天，以评估其对肾脏组织病理学和功能的影响。体外实验通过流式细胞术评估细胞活力、活性氧（ROS）水平和B[a]P积累。采用分子对接和细胞热位移分析（CETSA）确定三氯蔗糖与PGP的结合亲和力。此外，通过PCR、Western blotting和免疫组织化学分析PGP及其上游转录因子的表达。结果：三氯蔗糖和B[a]P联合暴露90天显著加剧小鼠肾功能障碍，表现为血清肌酐和尿素氮水平升高，这可通过ROS清除剂N-乙酰半胱氨酸（NAC）逆转。体外实验中，三氯蔗糖促进B[a]P在细胞内的积累，从而增强B[a]P诱导的细胞生长抑制和ROS产生。一致地，在HK2和HEK-293细胞中，PGP敲低增强了B[a]P积累。机制上，三氯蔗糖可直接结合PGP，竞争性抑制其外排能力，增加细胞内B[a]P滞留。长期联合暴露进一步下调PGP表达，可能通过减少其转录调控因子（PXR、NRF2和NF-kappaB）实现。结论：三氯蔗糖和B[a]P联合暴露通过损害PGP功能加剧肾损伤。机制上，三氯蔗糖抑制PGP活性，导致B[a]P在肾细胞内积累。这种积累触发氧化应激并抑制细胞生长，表明三氯蔗糖通过直接抑制PGP介导的解毒途径增强B[a]P诱导的肾毒性，从而强调评估这些化合物联合暴露相关毒性风险的关键必要性。
